baseline.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth slope occupies the centre, crossed by diffuse shallow linear traces. Broken gullies fringe the left and right edges. A sharply bounded, roughly quadrilateral raised patch with a flatter top lies in the southeast; several small irregular knobs lie near the west and south edges.
baseline.alternatives: The angular patch could be a modern building platform, spoil or water infrastructure. Gullies and linear traces may be erosion, tracks or terrain processing effects.
baseline.supportLimits: Most of the patch is measured, with scattered interpolated cells. The angular patch has measured support, but shape and age cannot be established from the model alone.

candidates.feature: Angular raised patch with relatively flat top
candidates.nextCheck: Compare with current and historical imagery, mapped structures, and original ground returns to identify construction or processing effects.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A broad, gently sloping central surface lies between two irregular drainage or erosion lines. Small rough patches and isolated knolls occur along the western edge. A sharply raised, angular mass sits near the southeast corner; aerial imagery shows exposed rock there. No coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
enriched.alternatives: The angular mass and scattered bumps are consistent with exposed bedrock and boulders. Edge lines resemble natural runoff channels; faint linear marks may be paths or land-use traces.
enriched.supportLimits: Most central cells are measured, with scattered interpolation. Terrain smoothing and tree cover limit fine shape interpretation; the aerial view and point-class overlay do not establish a built feature.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Several narrow branching incisions converge near the lower centre, forming a rough Y-shaped drainage pattern. Broad smooth flanks and a few irregular small bumps lie beside the channels. A short straight segment at the west edge meets one incision, but no coherent enclosure or platform is apparent.
baseline.alternatives: The incisions fit runoff erosion or drainage modification. The straight segment may be a field boundary, track or model artefact; the small bumps may be rock, vegetation remnants or spoil.
baseline.supportLimits: The main channel junction contains a band of interpolated cells, limiting confidence in its detailed shape. Broad surrounding ground is mostly measured.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Several narrow, branching incisions converge just below the patch centre and continue south. Small irregular protrusions occur beside the eastern branch and lower margins. The surrounding slopes are smooth to lightly rippled, without a clear bounded, level or symmetrical feature.
enriched.alternatives: The branching form and vegetated aerial corridor support drainage and erosion. Small protrusions could be rocks, tree-root ground effects or erosion remnants; a pale path crosses the western part.
enriched.supportLimits: The incisions coincide with substantial interpolation, so their sharpness and small adjoining forms need original-return checks before detailed interpretation. The point overlay adds no clear structure class evidence.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Dense, evenly spaced curved ridges wrap a broad rise on the west; shallower parallel ridges cover the east. A sharp north-south break divides them, meeting an east-west line near the lower third. A compact rounded rise interrupts the eastern ridges near the upper centre-right.
baseline.alternatives: Repeated ridges suggest agricultural cultivation or terracing. The straight breaks could be a track, boundary or drainage. The compact rise could be exposed rock, field clearance, soil accumulation or a natural knoll.
baseline.supportLimits: The broad surfaces are mostly measured; intermittent interpolation follows the central break and lower line. The compact rise is in largely measured terrain, but the imagery alone cannot resolve its origin.

candidates.feature: Compact rounded rise amid parallel ridges
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and aerial imagery for rock, agricultural clearance or recent disturbance.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Closely spaced curved ridges cover the western field; finer parallel rows occupy the eastern planted plot. A boundary track runs north-south near the centre and another crosses east-west in the lower half. A small rounded rise interrupts the rows in the northeast quadrant.
enriched.alternatives: The repeated ridges and straight plot edges indicate cultivation or earthworks tied to current land use. The isolated rise could be bedrock, a spoil pile, a tree-associated mound or grading disturbance.
enriched.supportLimits: Most cells are measured; some boundary and rise-edge cells are interpolated. The aerial image shows active planting and vegetation around the rise, limiting ground interpretation. The point overlay does not resolve its origin.

candidates.feature: Small rounded rise amid planted rows
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and field imagery for a real bounded rise, then compare with cultivation and bedrock patterns.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: A largely smooth surface contains several isolated small rises and shallow depressions. One compact irregular cluster lies just east of the patch centre; a more prominent small rise lies in the northwest. Very faint straight traces run between some of the bumps, without a clear enclosure or platform.
baseline.alternatives: The bumps may be stones, clearance heaps, vegetation remnants, small natural knolls or modern disturbance. The faint traces may be tracks, cultivation lines or processing artefacts.
baseline.supportLimits: The central cluster and most surrounding ground have measured model support, with only sparse isolated interpolation. Their small size still makes interpretation uncertain without raw returns and independent imagery.

candidates.feature: Small irregular cluster of rises east of centre
candidates.nextCheck: Compare original ground returns, aerial imagery and mapped surface features to distinguish stones or clearance from terrain-processing effects.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A largely smooth open surface is crossed by a faint north-south track. Several small, separate rounded or jagged protrusions flank it, with a larger irregular rise in the northwest quadrant. The wider view shows many similar outcrops around the patch, rather than a coherent bounded arrangement.
enriched.alternatives: Aerial imagery shows pale exposed stone at the protrusions, consistent with bedrock or boulders. The line is a visible track; small depressions and humps may reflect natural rock weathering or passage.
enriched.supportLimits: Ground support is predominantly measured. The imagery and point-class overlay do not demonstrate structures, and small forms may be altered by terrain smoothing; original returns would be needed for any stronger reading.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: Several irregular clusters of sharp, small rises occupy the northern half, largest near the east centre; isolated bumps and a faint curving track appear elsewhere. No continuous enclosure, level platform, or regular plan is clear across illumination directions.
baseline.alternatives: Natural exposed rock and field clearance could account for the clusters; the eastern curve may be a modern track.
baseline.supportLimits: Many sharp rises coincide with interpolated cells, particularly in the eastern cluster, so their edges and separations require measured-return checks.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A group of sharp, irregular raised forms occupies the northeast quarter, with isolated smaller knobs to the west and south. Most of the patch is smooth, gently sloping ground. Tracks cross the southeast and run just outside the eastern edge. No continuous bank, enclosure or level platform is clear.
enriched.alternatives: The raised forms coincide with exposed pale rocks in the aerial image and similar rocky groups nearby. Minor pits and streaks may reflect vegetation, grazing, tracks or terrain interpolation around rock edges.
enriched.supportLimits: Measured support dominates, but interpolation clusters around the sharpest outcrops. The RGB image and class overlay show surface context, not age or purpose. The missing terrain beside the nearby water body lies outside the patch.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A sinuous north–south incised line branches near the top, with broad smooth lobes on either side and a shorter east–west break across the middle. Its irregular width and branching continue across the patch. Small isolated knolls lie to the northeast.
baseline.alternatives: Drainage or erosion and adjacent natural slope changes explain the pattern; a track or field boundary might contribute to the east–west break.
baseline.supportLimits: The channel-like line and its junctions contain many interpolated cells, with a small missing area near the bottom. Their fine edges are uncertain.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A branching, irregular north–south incision crosses the centre, with a small missing-data pocket near its lower end. The west side has rounded slopes and a few short ridges; the east side has rough ground and nearly horizontal narrow bands. The watercourse continues well beyond the patch.
enriched.alternatives: The incision follows a vegetated drainage line in the aerial images. East-side bands could be cultivation, erosion or tracks. Isolated bumps coincide with rocky or vegetated ground; no closed or repeated structural arrangement is clear.
enriched.supportLimits: Interpolation follows much of the narrow channel and rough patches, while the southern pocket is missing. Channel-edge shapes may therefore be smoothed or distorted. The aerial image helps identify drainage but does not date the bands.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: Most of the patch is smooth. A broad, faint, elongated rise lies southwest of centre, with a softer low strip along its western and southern sides; its perimeter is incomplete. Small isolated bumps and a narrow north–south line occur near the northeast edge.
baseline.alternatives: The elongated rise could be a natural slope lobe or shallow drainage divide. The northeast line may be a track or field edge.
baseline.supportLimits: The broad rise is predominantly measured, but its relief is subtle and the images alone do not resolve its origin.

candidates.feature: Broad elongated rise with incomplete low margin
candidates.nextCheck: Examine ground-return profiles across and along the rise, then compare the surrounding terrain and dated imagery for a natural slope or recent disturbance.

enriched.visibleGeometry: The centre is smooth open ground with a broad, weakly raised lobe or shallow slope change in the southwest half. Small irregular knobs occur near the north edge and at the south edge. A faint track cuts diagonally across the northern part; another lies near the east edge. No sharp perimeter or regular internal divisions appear.
enriched.alternatives: The broad relief may be an ordinary natural knoll or drainage-side undulation. Pale aerial patches correspond to scattered exposed stone; linear traces align with current tracks. The subtle lobe lacks a coherent constructed outline.
enriched.supportLimits: Ground support is mostly measured, with scattered interpolation around stones and southern rough ground. The lobe is low contrast across derivatives and has no distinct boundary, so its precise extent is uncertain.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A long irregular break runs west–east across the lower middle, bending upward to the east. Several broad shallow lobes meet it from north and south. The northern surface is rougher and the southern surface smoother; no closed or regular outline is clear.
baseline.alternatives: A natural drainage or terrace edge, field boundary, or track could produce the break. The lobes may reflect local slope and runoff.
baseline.supportLimits: Interpolated cells concentrate along the break and scattered rough spots, weakening interpretation of its fine shape; most broad surfaces are measured.

enriched.visibleGeometry: An irregular but continuous east–west break in slope arcs across the lower middle of the patch. The ground north of it is rougher and more finely textured, while the south is smoother with broad shallow undulations. Scattered small knobs lie mainly north of the break; no enclosed outline appears.
enriched.alternatives: The break closely follows the present unpaved road and tree line in the aerial image. The adjacent relief could reflect road cutting, drainage and natural slope change. Small knobs may be rocks or tree-related terrain artefacts.
enriched.supportLimits: Interpolation concentrates along the road and around several northern trees, limiting fine interpretation of the break. It continues beyond the patch in both directions. The point-class image adds no clear structural class pattern here.

references.name: Anta da Aldeia da Mata/ Tapadão 1/Couto dos Pucarinhos

baseline.visibleGeometry: A cluster of short, angular ridges and raised blocks occupies the northwest quadrant, with an isolated small raised block to its south. A narrow curving line runs just east of the cluster. A separate low rounded rise lies farther south near the line; the remaining ground is subdued.
baseline.alternatives: Standing or collapsed modern structures, rock piles, vegetation artifacts, a track and ordinary ground disturbance could account for the shapes.
baseline.supportLimits: The angular cluster overlaps a dense patch of interpolated cells, so its sharp shapes cannot be accepted without source-ground inspection. Most surrounding ground is measured.

candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original classified returns and current or historical imagery for buildings, rock piles and interpolation effects.

enriched.visibleGeometry: An irregular cluster of high, angular ridges and blocks occupies the northwest quarter; a curved track passes its east side. A smaller isolated rise lies farther south. Similar rough outcrops occur across the surrounding terrain. The aerial view shows exposed grey rock, scattered shrubs and the track.
enriched.alternatives: Natural bedrock outcrop and loose stone are the strongest explanation. The southern rise may be another rock exposure. Some apparent straight segments could be chance joints or low walls; the nearby route is modern access.
enriched.supportLimits: The main rough cluster contains many interpolated cells. Its exact relief and apparent internal edges need original return checks. Aerial detail does not establish construction or age.

baseline.visibleGeometry: A broad, curving break in slope crosses the patch from the left edge toward the upper-right side. Its upper side is irregular and stippled with small bumps; the lower side is comparatively smooth with scattered low hummocks. A faint straight line crosses the upper-right area.
baseline.alternatives: A natural drainage or slope margin, track or field edge and vegetation-related roughness fit the pattern. The isolated hummocks may be ordinary surface variation.
baseline.supportLimits: Interpolation follows much of the curving break and several bump clusters. Those details require raw-return confirmation; the smooth lower area is mainly measured.

enriched.visibleGeometry: A broad smooth slope meets a rougher, tree-covered surface along a curving east-west break near the patch middle. Several small knolls and angular rough spots lie on both sides. The aerial view places a dirt route along the break; rough areas coincide with trees and exposed stone.
enriched.alternatives: The break is plausibly a route cut or field edge following natural relief. Rough spots may be bedrock, vegetation effects or erosion. No coherent enclosed or platform-like form stands apart from these patterns.
enriched.supportLimits: Scattered interpolated cells coincide with trees and the rough break. Fine shape and small protrusions cannot be trusted without source returns. Aerial imagery shows current surface cover only.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Regular, close-spaced curved ridges occupy the upper-left field; parallel fine ridges also cross the upper-right and lower areas. Straight north-south and east-west linear breaks meet near the centre, separating differently textured ground. A small bright lump lies at the junction.
baseline.alternatives: Cultivation rows, field boundaries, a track or drainage line and a small boundary feature explain the pattern.
baseline.supportLimits: The boundary lines and central junction include interpolated cells. Most cultivated surfaces are measured, though small scattered gaps remain.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Regular, closely spaced cultivation ridges fill much of the west and south. Straight field boundaries meet a curving east-west track near the centre. A small narrow protrusion at that junction aligns with a tree or hedge in the aerial view. The northeast field is rougher with scattered trees.
enriched.alternatives: The lines and ridges match agricultural plots, ploughing and access routes. The junction protrusion may be a tree base, boundary stone or drainage/track feature. No distinct older enclosure or mound is apparent.
enriched.supportLimits: Interpolation is concentrated along hedges, tracks and trees, including the junction. Their small relief forms need source returns to distinguish ground from canopy or smoothing effects.

baseline.visibleGeometry: Two nearly parallel linear boundaries frame a broad, gently textured strip across the patch. Regular cultivation ridges lie above and below it. A discrete small rounded rise sits near the upper boundary at about x310, y99; a few smaller bumps occur near the lower-right edge.
baseline.alternatives: Field margins, track edges or drainage features explain the long lines. The isolated rise could be a tree base, soil or rock pile, or agricultural feature.
baseline.supportLimits: Interpolation follows both long boundaries and scattered patches within the strip. The rise is beside an interpolated boundary, so its form needs raw-return verification.

candidates.feature: Small isolated rounded rise beside field boundary
candidates.nextCheck: Inspect original ground returns and imagery to distinguish a persistent mound from a tree base, pile or boundary disturbance.

enriched.visibleGeometry: Two gently curving, nearly parallel field boundaries run across the patch, enclosing an area with scattered tree-related roughness. Fine cultivation ridges fill the ground above and below. A small raised angular spot near the north boundary corresponds to exposed rock in the aerial view; the lower boundary follows a dirt route.
enriched.alternatives: Agricultural boundaries, cultivation and access paths explain the dominant lines. The isolated rise appears to be rock. Tree cover and occasional stones account for the irregular relief between boundaries.
enriched.supportLimits: Interpolated cells cluster on both boundaries and around tree positions. The slight field roughness is sensitive to ground-return gaps; neither image set establishes construction or age.
